question: You are reviewing a pull request. Below are the unified diff and the resulting files (changed files plus unchanged context files). List EVERY defect the change introduces or exposes, one per line, and briefly say why each is a problem. Report only real defects, not style preferences.

tasks.title: Partial refunds with idempotency (4 files, API + service + store)

provenance.note: SYNTHETIC: authored for xllm as a realistic multi-file change with defects planted by the author. Not derived from a real incident or repository; no real-world provenance is claimed. Real retrospective bugs are added with `xllm-bench import-cases`.

defects.description: Refund cap compares only against the full payment amount, not amount minus already refunded, so repeated partial refunds can exceed the payment.
refunded_cents/refund_count are computed from a stale read of the payment and written back non-atomically; concurrent refunds overwrite each other and bypass the cap.
The processor refund (side effect) happens before the idempotency key is recorded, so a crash/timeout between them lets a retry refund twice.
A missing Idempotency-Key is undefined and matches any earlier refund with an undefined key, so a later legitimate refund is silently swallowed and returns the old refund.
Math.floor(Number(amount) * 100) truncates binary floating-point results (19.99 * 100 = 1998.999...), refunding a cent less than requested.
The audit actor is taken from the request body before the authenticated user, so any caller can forge who performed the refund.

tasks.title: Per-tenant project cache layer (4 files, cache + service + middleware)

provenance.note: SYNTHETIC: authored for xllm as a realistic multi-file change with defects planted by the author. Not derived from a real incident or repository; no real-world provenance is claimed. Real retrospective bugs are added with `xllm-bench import-cases`.

defects.description: projectKey ignores tenantId, so two tenants with the same project id share one cache entry and read each other's data.
expiresAt = now() + ttlSeconds mixes seconds with milliseconds: entries expire after ~300 ms, and the 24h negative entry after ~86 s.
The cache is invalidated before the DB write commits; a concurrent read repopulates the old value which then persists until TTL (stale cache after update).
Missing projects are cached for 24 hours and never invalidated on create, so a newly created project keeps returning 404.
The cache returns the same object reference; addMember mutates req.project.members in place, corrupting the cached entry even if the DB update fails.

tasks.title: Cursor pagination for the events API (4 files incl. SQL migration)

provenance.note: SYNTHETIC: authored for xllm as a realistic multi-file change with defects planted by the author. Not derived from a real incident or repository; no real-world provenance is claimed. Real retrospective bugs are added with `xllm-bench import-cases`.

defects.description: The cursor is only created_at; rows sharing a timestamp are skipped or repeated across pages because there is no unique tiebreaker (id) in the cursor and ORDER BY.
Rows are ordered DESC but the cursor filter uses created_at > cursor, which returns newer rows than the cursor (wrong direction) instead of older ones.

defects.pattern: limit ?\+ ?1|extra row|has.?more|empty (last )?page|exactly (limit|a full page)|next_cursor.*(non-?null|even when|always|exactly)|full page
defects.description: next_cursor is emitted whenever a full page is returned; without fetching limit+1 the final page that exactly fills the limit yields a cursor to an empty page.
The decoded, client-controlled cursor value is interpolated directly into the SQL string (SQL injection); it is also never validated after JSON.parse.

defects.pattern: concurrently.*(transaction|begin)|(transaction|begin).*concurrently|cannot run inside a transaction|CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
defects.description: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside BEGIN/COMMIT in PostgreSQL; the migration fails.
The previous Math.min(limit, 200) cap was dropped: clients can request arbitrarily large or negative limits.

tasks.title: At-least-once queue worker with retries and dead-lettering (4 files)

provenance.note: SYNTHETIC: authored for xllm as a realistic multi-file change with defects planted by the author. Not derived from a real incident or repository; no real-world provenance is claimed. Real retrospective bugs are added with `xllm-bench import-cases`.

defects.description: Messages are acknowledged before the handler runs; a crash (or a handler failure whose retry publish fails) loses the message, contradicting the at-least-once contract.
Attempt counts live in a per-process Map, so they reset on restart and are not shared across workers; with republished copies a poison message may never reach MAX_ATTEMPTS.
Backoff grows as 500ms * 2^attempt with no cap or jitter: the last attempts wait minutes/hours and synchronized retries cause thundering herds.
The dead-letter record keeps the error and ids but not the message body, so the failed work cannot be inspected or replayed.
A failing publishDelayed/deadLetter inside the mapped promise rejects Promise.all for the whole batch with no recovery, and because messages were already acked the affected ones are gone.

The handler records welcome_sent_at before sending; a send failure leaves the user marked as welcomed and the retry cannot rely on it, while redelivery without a check sends duplicates (no idempotency guard).

tasks.title: Home-grown bearer-token auth + role policy (4 files)

provenance.note: SYNTHETIC: authored for xllm as a realistic multi-file change with defects planted by the author. Not derived from a real incident or repository; no real-world provenance is claimed. Real retrospective bugs are added with `xllm-bench import-cases`.

defects.description: payload.exp is in seconds but is compared to Date.now() in milliseconds, so tokens effectively never expire.
Signature verification only runs when header.alg is HS256; any other alg (including none) skips verification, so forged unsigned tokens are accepted.
The signature is compared with !==/=== instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, allowing timing attacks.
hasRole joins roles into a string and uses includes, so "admin" matches "billing_admin" or "superadmin-readonly"; it should test array membership.
isPublic uses startsWith on the raw path: /publicity, /public-admin and unnormalised paths such as /public/../admin skip authentication.
The full Authorization header (the bearer token) is written to the central log pipeline at debug level.

tasks.title: Config loader refactor touching 9 files (long mostly-mechanical diff with buried defects)

provenance.note: SYNTHETIC: authored for xllm as a realistic multi-file change with defects planted by the author. Not derived from a real incident or repository; no real-world provenance is claimed. Real retrospective bugs are added with `xllm-bench import-cases`.

defects.description: MAX_RETRIES is no longer parsed: it becomes a string, so withRetry computes maxRetries + 1 as string concatenation ("5" + 1 = "51") and loops far too many times.
FEATURE_NEW_SEARCH=false (any non-empty string) now enables the feature because the === 'true' check was replaced by !!.
Object.assign(defaults, ...) mutates the shared defaults module object (the previous code copied into {}), so overrides leak into the defaults for every other importer and later load() calls.
fromFile now swallows every error (missing file, bad JSON) and returns {}, so a broken config silently falls back to defaults instead of failing at startup.
